issues.legal_issue: The court-fee valuation of a landlord-tenant eviction suit is determined by the plaint’s allegations and relief, not by a denial of the landlord’s title in the written statement.
material_facts: The plaintiffs’ plaint alleged that they owned the property, that the defendant was their tenant, and that he was in arrears of rent; it sought his eviction.
The plaintiffs valued the suit by reference to the rent for twelve months.
The defendant denied the landlord-tenant relationship and claimed that the transaction was a loan secured by documents, including a purported tenancy agreement.
The trial court ordered the plaintiffs to pay ad valorem court fees based on the property’s market value because it considered that title would need to be decided fully.
issues.conclusion: The suit was to be valued as an eviction suit on the basis of rent, and the defendant’s denial of title did not require payment of ad valorem court fees based on the property’s market value.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 7 of the Court Fees Act, 1870, court fees in a suit between landlord and tenant for recovery of immovable property are computed by reference to the rent payable for the year before presentation of the plaint. As stated in Sathappa Chettiar v. Ramanathan Chettiar, the court-fee question is determined by the allegations in the plaint and the relief sought, not by the written statement or the eventual decision on the merits. The character of this suit therefore remained an eviction suit despite the defendant’s denial of title.

predicates.landlord_tenant_eviction_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking recovery of property from a person alleged to be a tenant.
predicates.plaint_alleges_landlord_tenant_relations: The plaintiff alleged in the plaint that the plaintiff was the landlord and the defendant was the tenant.
predicates.plaint_seeks_eviction: The plaintiff asked the court to evict the defendant from the property.
predicates.court_fee_valuation_uses_rent_basis: The court fees are computed by reference to the rent for the relevant year rather than the property’s market value.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff brings an eviction suit alleging a landlord-tenant relationship and seeking eviction, the court-fee valuation uses the rent basis.
